message.content:
You're implementing Phase 6 (build plan step B2) of the SFCC-83/84 (Recently Viewed) build on branch `feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed` in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Three prior phases just completed and you'll consume all three — read each of these files in full first, they are your ground truth, more reliable than any paraphrase below:

- `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` — returns `{hasRecentlyViewed, recentlyViewedIds, markProductViewed}`.
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` — given a list of IDs, fetches real product data (capped at 24 internally already — you don't need to cap anything yourself).
- `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — maps one product to card props (`selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` — confirm the exact export name by reading the file). **Known, already-flagged gap in this file: `badge` is always `undefined`** — the Commerce API endpoint it reads from doesn't expose the field this session could find. This is not something to fix in this step; just be aware a card's badge will never show yet, that's expected, not a bug in your own code.

Also read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/index.tsx` in full (just completed too) — your target render component. Confirm its exact prop names (`title`, `itemCountLabel`, `cards`) by reading it directly.

Read the plan at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` next — step B2 has extensive detail: route placement reasoning, the `Seo` `noIndex` gotcha, and the empty-state precedent research (a full copy table already derived from the real `EmptyCart` component).

**Create** `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` — a thin container page:

1. Call `useRecentlyViewedHistory()` for `recentlyViewedIds`. Call `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s hook/utility with those IDs to get real product data. Map each result through `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard` (filtering out any `null`s — same hard-gate contract every mapper in this codebase uses). Render `<ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid>` with the resulting `cards` array.

2. **Item count — build it with real ICU pluralization, not string interpolation.** Use `useIntl()`'s `formatMessage` with a `plural` ICU selector (e.g. `{count, plural, one {# Item} other {# Items}}`) to build the `itemCountLabel` string from `cards.length`, and pass that to the grid's `itemCountLabel` prop. This was explicitly decided this session — do not ship a naive `` `${count} Items` `` template.

3. **Title** — "Recently Viewed", via `useIntl()`, matching this codebase's existing i18n message conventions (look at how `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` or another existing page defines its own `defineMessages`/message IDs and follow the same pattern).

4. **Empty state** — when `cards.length === 0` (or `recentlyViewedIds.length === 0`, whichever is the more correct signal — reason about which one, they should be equivalent unless every ID failed to hydrate), render a heading + `isRegistered`-branched body copy + CTA(s), not a blank page. Use this exact copy, derived from the plan's own research into the real `EmptyCart` component (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/partials/empty-cart.jsx`) — read that file too, to match its actual structure/component usage (icon placement, `Stack`/`Center` layout, `Button as={Link}` pattern) rather than just the words:

| Piece | Copy |
|---|---|
| Heading | "You haven't viewed anything yet." |
| Body (registered) | "Continue shopping to start building your history." |
| Body (guest) | "Sign in to keep track of your history, or continue shopping." |
| CTA 1 (both) | "Continue Shopping" → `/` |
| CTA 2 (guest only) | "Sign In" → `/account` |

No icon — checked earlier this session, nothing in this project's icon barrel fits, and forcing an unrelated one would be worse than omitting it. `isRegistered` — same `useCustomerType()` hook `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and `use-einstein.js:449` already use.

5. **SEO — `noindex, nofollow`, via `Seo`'s children, not its `noIndex` prop.** Base `Seo`'s `noIndex` prop emits `noindex` only, no `nofollow` — confirmed by reading `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/seo/index.jsx` directly. Pattern:
```tsx
<Seo title={...} description={...}>
  <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow" />
</Seo>
```
Do not also set the `noIndex` prop alongside this — that would emit two competing `robots` tags. Follow the same `<Seo>` usage pattern as `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx` for everything else about how this page mounts it.

6. **`getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed'`** — check how the four other pages using this pattern define it (grep for `getTemplateName` across `overrides/app/pages/`) and match the exact convention/placement.

7. **No data-fetching hook inside `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` itself** — it already doesn't have one (confirmed, it's presentational); just don't add one when wiring this up. All fetching happens in this container.

**Add** `RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE = '/recently-viewed'` to `overrides/app/constants/index.ts` (a new constant — Phase 1 already added `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` to this same file; add yours alongside it, don't touch that one).

**Modify** `overrides/app/routes.tsx` — add one route entry. Read the file's current real content first (small file, quick read) — it has an existing `/preview` entry positioned deliberately after the base `..._routes` spread and before the `/:slug` catch-all, with an inline comment explaining why. Add `/recently-viewed` adjacent to `/preview` (either immediately before or after it — functionally equivalent, pick whichever reads more naturally next to the existing comments), with your own one-line comment following the same style as the existing entries' comments, stating that this route has no ordering constraint versus the base array (no base route shares this path) and just needs to land before the `/:slug` catch-all.

After all changes: run `npx tsc --noEmit` (must be clean, modulo the one already-known, separately-in-progress `recommended-products/index.tsx` issue — check first whether that's resolved by the time you run this; if not, confirm your own files produce zero errors and note the pre-existing one is out of your scope) and `npm run build` (the plan specifically calls this out: a bad `loadable`/route wiring can fail at build even when `tsc` is clean). Write a `.test.tsx` covering: cards render when history exists; empty state renders when it doesn't, correctly branched on `isRegistered` (both branches); item count pluralizes correctly (test both `1 Item` and a plural count). Mock `useRecentlyViewedHistory`, the product-fetch utility, and the mapper at the smallest surface, matching this codebase's established mocking conventions elsewhere in this build (look at `recommended-products/index.test.tsx`'s pre-existing mock style, even though that file itself is mid-revision by another process right now — its overall mocking approach/conventions are still valid to copy).

**Verify against the real running app** — it's already running at `http://localhost:3000`, do not start or restart it. Curl `/recently-viewed` directly and confirm: 200 response, the page actually renders (not a 404/fallback), and the response body contains exactly one `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">` tag (grep the raw HTML for it). Also confirm the empty state renders correctly for a fresh session with no view history (which is what a bare curl request naturally is) — you should see the empty-state heading text in the raw SSR'd HTML.

If you hit genuine ambiguity, decide from existing codebase precedent and list the decision with reasoning in your final report — do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO.

Do not modify any file not named above (do not touch `recommended-products/index.tsx`, any hook, or any util other than reading them). Do not run `git commit`. Report back: what you built, the empty-state/SEO/route verification results concretely (paste the actual curl-confirmed meta tag), tsc/build/test results, and your list of autonomous decisions.

1	/**
2	 * The "given IDs, fetch real product data" half of SFCC-83/84's interim Recently Viewed data
3	 * source (build plan §2, "Interim data source" — Einstein is "Not Deployed" on every real
4	 * Zimmermann site, so this build ships against a browser-tracked view-history stand-in instead).
5	 * The companion piece is `useRecentlyViewedHistory`
6	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts`), which supplies the `ids` this hook
7	 * consumes — every product this hook returns is real, live Commerce Cloud data; only the list of
8	 * *which* IDs to fetch is sourced from this browser's own tracked history rather than Einstein.
9	 *
10	 * Wraps `useProducts` (`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`, confirmed real export at
11	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js`, re-exported from
12	 * the package root — the same hook already used at
13	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:334`), which calls the Shopper Products
14	 * `getProducts` endpoint. Parameters (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [
15	 * 'prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations']`) match the combination already confirmed
16	 * correct three independent times this build (Einstein's own `fetchRecProductDetails`
17	 * — `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505` — the PLP quick-test mapper,
18	 * and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's real-product search call).
19	 *
20	 * **The 24-ID cap is a real, hard API limit, not a preference.** Confirmed directly in the SDK's
21	 * own doc comment: `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/hooks/ShopperProducts/query.js:29`
22	 * — *"The maximum number of productIDs that can be requested are 24."* — restated independently
23	 * in `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type-declaration prose
24	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:58802`: *"hydrate a list of products
25	 * (max 24)"*). Marcel's explicit decision: cap to the first `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST`
26	 * ids, don't batch into multiple requests — a shopper with more than 24 tracked IDs simply never
27	 * gets the tail of their history fetched by this hook.
28	 *
29	 * **SDK param widening for `ids`.** `getProductsQueryParameters.ids` types as `Array<string>`
30	 * throughout `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` (confirmed at `index.esm.d.ts:57797` and `:58753`), but the
31	 * real, working base SFCC call this build models (`use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`)
32	 * passes a comma-joined string (`ids.join(',')`) straight through — the SDK forwards it verbatim
33	 * into the query string regardless of the declared array type. This file follows the exact same
34	 * precedent already used elsewhere in this codebase for this exact field:
35	 * `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:339`
36	 * (`ids: childVariantIds.join(',') as unknown as string[]`, commented there as "SDK param
37	 * widening").
38	 */
39	import { useProducts } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
40	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
41	
42	/**
43	 * Hard per-request limit on the Shopper Products `getProducts` endpoint — see this file's own
44	 * docblock above for the two independent SDK citations confirming this number. Not a UX/product
45	 * choice, and not adjustable client-side.
46	 */
47	const GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST = 24;
48	
49	export type RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult = {
50	  /**
51	   * Real Shopper Products data for as many of the requested (capped) `ids` as the API actually
52	   * returned, **re-ordered to match `ids`'s own order** — the API's own response order is not
53	   * documented or guaranteed to match request order, so this hook does the re-ordering rather
54	   * than assume it. An id the API didn't return at all (e.g. offline or deleted since it was
55	   * viewed) is silently dropped, not left as a hole in the array.
56	   */
57	  products: readonly ShopperProductsTypes.Product[];
58	  /** `true` only while a real fetch is in flight for a non-empty id list — deliberately `false`,
59	   *  not the underlying query's own (potentially permanently-pending) loading state, when there
60	   *  are no ids to fetch at all, since no request is ever made in that case. */
61	  isLoading: boolean;
62	};
63	
64	/**
65	 * Given a list of product IDs (most-recent-first, per `useRecentlyViewedHistory`), fetches real,
66	 * live Commerce Cloud product data for them.
67	 *
68	 * @param ids - Product IDs to fetch, most-recent-first. A list longer than
69	 *   `GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST` is truncated to the first N (Marcel's cap-don't-batch
70	 *   decision) — the endpoint itself has no way to serve more in a single call.
71	 * @returns `products` — real product data for the requested ids, re-ordered to match `ids` and
72	 *   with any id the API didn't return dropped. `isLoading` — whether a real fetch is in flight.
73	 */
74	export const useRecentlyViewedProductFetch = (ids: readonly string[]): RecentlyViewedProductFetchResult => {
75	  const cappedIds = ids.slice(0, GET_PRODUCTS_MAX_IDS_PER_REQUEST);
76	
77	  const { data, isLoading: queryIsLoading } = useProducts(
78	    {
79	      parameters: {
80	        // SDK param widening -- see this file's own docblock for why a comma-joined string is
81	        // correct here despite the declared `Array<string>` type.
82	        ids: cappedIds.join(',') as unknown as string[],
83	        allImages: true,
84	        perPricebook: true,
85	        expand: ['prices', 'promotions', 'images', 'variations'],
86	      },
87	    },
88	    {
89	      // Matches the existing precedent at product-detail/index.tsx:347 for this same hook: don't
90	      // fire a request at all when there's nothing to ask for.
91	      enabled: cappedIds.length > 0,
92	    },
93	  );
94	
95	  const productsById = new Map((data?.data ?? []).map((product) => [product.id, product] as const));
96	  const products = cappedIds
97	    .map((id) => productsById.get(id))
98	    .filter((product): product is ShopperProductsTypes.Product => product !== undefined);
99	
100	  return {
101	    products,
102	    // A disabled query (no ids) never transitions out of its initial loading state on some
103	    // TanStack Query versions/configurations -- AND against `cappedIds.length > 0` so "loading"
104	    // never lies about a fetch that was never actually started.
105	    isLoading: cappedIds.length > 0 && queryIsLoading,
106	  };
107	};
108

1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed product to the FULL `ZimmProductCard` props Recently Viewed's Full
3	 * History page (SFCC-84) renders — badge, size chips, was/now pricing and a multi-image gallery,
4	 * i.e. the `plp` variation's already-shipped shape, not `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s narrower
5	 * image-only rail shape (SFCC-83's `recentlyViewed` variation). Both mappers read the same
6	 * underlying input — a plain Commerce API `Product` from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
7	 * `getProducts` call — but produce deliberately different output shapes for two deliberately
8	 * different surfaces; see that mapper's own docblock for the rail's narrower contract and why it
9	 * stops at image-only.
10	 *
11	 * Added per the build plan's B2 discussion (finding 41b): "reuse the rail's mapper" was the
12	 * original, incorrect assumption for this page — `recentlyViewedCard.ts` cannot produce this
13	 * shape by its own design (image-only, no price, no gallery), so a second, separate mapper is
14	 * required. Per Jasmijn's SFCC-84 comment, the Full History card's default state is "image, name,
15	 * badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon" — exactly the `plp` variation's shape, which is why
16	 * this mapper's output includes `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` directly (unlike
17	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s `RecentlyViewedCard`, which deliberately excludes both as its rail
18	 * container's job) — mirroring `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult`, which
19	 * bakes in the same two fields for the same reason: its output is meant to be spread straight
20	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` with nothing left for a caller to add.
21	 *
22	 * Modelled on `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s general style/docblock conventions (no React/react-intl
23	 * import, `formatPrice` injected as a parameter, same hard `null`-gate contract for a product
24	 * with no usable name/image) and on `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`
25	 * (the closest existing precedent producing this exact `plp`-variation output shape from a real
26	 * product). Ported, not imported, from both — a genuinely separate, self-contained module with
27	 * its own local type aliases, the same relationship `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already has to
28	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` (see that file's own docblock).
29	 *
30	 * **What's ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`, and what changed:**
31	 * `selectGalleryImages`/`selectSizeChipValues` are re-pointed at `product.imageGroups`/
32	 * `product.variationAttributes` directly (the plain `Product` shape) in place of a
33	 * `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named fields — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`/
34	 * `VariationAttribute` shapes are the same `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` types either way (confirmed
35	 * directly against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`), so the
36	 * picking/mapping logic itself needed no change, only the input type.
37	 *
38	 * **Primary-image resolution is NOT ported from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
39	 * `toCardImage(hit.image)`** — a plain `getProducts` `Product` has no equivalent flat `image`
40	 * field; that is a Search-hit-only convenience field. Instead this mirrors `recentlyViewedCard.ts`
41	 * `selectPrimaryImage` (`viewType: 'medium'` `imageGroups` lookup, required non-empty `alt`) — the
42	 * already-established, correct approach for this exact input shape.
43	 *
44	 * **Price handling is deliberately NOT copied from `productListCardMapper.ts`.** That mapper reads
45	 * the flat `hit.price` field for `currentPrice` while leaving `originalPrice` unset entirely — had
46	 * it called `getPriceData(hit).listPrice` for `originalPrice` while keeping `hit.price` for
47	 * `currentPrice`, the two would risk disagreeing on a multi-variant product, since `getPriceData`
48	 * internally sources its own `currentPrice` from `findLowestPrice()`, not from a flat `price`
49	 * field. Both `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` here come from one `getPriceData(product)` call
50	 * (base SFCC, `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:123-170`,
51	 * confirmed by reading it directly) so the two halves can never disagree. `originalPrice` is only
52	 * ever set when that same call's `isOnSale` is `true` — a not-on-sale product must not render a
53	 * crossed-out price identical to its current one.
54	 *
55	 * **Badge — a real, found gap, not silently papered over.** `productListCardMapper.ts` reads
56	 * `hit.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge` off a Search hit's custom index field. Checked directly
57	 * against `commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own type declaration for the plain `Product` shape
58	 * (`node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts:59783-59835`, the exact block backing
59	 * `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`): there is no typed `c_productBadges` field there — only a
60	 * generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, which would let `product.c_productBadges`
61	 * compile without error but proves nothing about whether the real `getProducts` endpoint (a
62	 * hydration endpoint, not the search-index endpoint `c_productBadges` is confirmed on) actually
63	 * populates this custom, index-only attribute. `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own `getProducts`
64	 * call requests no expand parameter that obviously corresponds to custom attributes either.
65	 * Rather than read a field with no confirmed backing, `badge` is left `undefined` below — see that
66	 * assignment's own comment. This is a real, unresolved gap, not a design choice: if Full History
67	 * needs badges to actually render, confirming whether `getProducts` carries this field needs a
68	 * live check against a real badged product in a running environment, the same "verify in the
69	 * running app" caveat the build plan's own B2 discussion already states for was/now pricing.
70	 */
71	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
72	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
73	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
74	import type {
75	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
76	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
77	  ZimmProductCardImage,
78	} from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
79	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
80	
81	/**
82	 * The real Commerce API `Product` this mapper reads — the same `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
83	 * `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` produces and `recentlyViewedCard.ts` also consumes. Named
84	 * locally (rather than importing `RecentlyViewedProduct` from that sibling module) so this stays
85	 * a genuinely separate, self-contained module — matching how this whole file is itself "ported,
86	 * not imported" from its own two precedents.
87	 */
88	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product;
89	
90	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl —
91	 *  same shape as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `FormatPrice`, redeclared locally for the same
92	 *  separate-module reason as `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct` above. */
93	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
94	
95	/**
96	 * The full `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard` props this mapper produces — badge, size chips,
97	 * was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, heading level and variation all included. Mirrors
98	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` (unexported from that file, so
99	 * redeclared here rather than imported) — this mapper's output is meant to be spread straight
100	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` by its page container (SFCC-84's Full History page, not yet built)
101	 * with nothing left to add, the same convenience that shape already gives PLP's own page.
102	 */
103	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
104	
105	/** The correctly-sized product image view for the required `primaryImage` slot — same constant,
106	 *  same reasoning, as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`: never serve an
107	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance). */
108	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
109	
110	/** The variation-attribute id this mapper reads for size chips — named per conventions.md's
111	 *  no-magic-strings rule. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectSizeChipValues`, which this is
112	 *  ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file. */
113	const SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'size';
114	
115	/**
116	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
117	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
118	 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s
119	 * catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`, a shorthand ambient module
120	 * declaration that types the whole module `any`, so `getPriceData`'s real return is implicitly
121	 * `any`. Declaring a local, narrow type for the fields actually read — rather than letting that
122	 * `any` propagate into this module's own types — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
123	 * narrow-local-type pattern for the same untyped function (typescript.md's no-`any` rule). This
124	 * is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee: TypeScript allows
125	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
126	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
127	 */
128	type SfccPriceData = {
129	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
130	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
131	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
132	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
133	  currentPrice: number;
134	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
135	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
136	  listPrice: number | undefined;
137	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
138	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */
139	  isOnSale: boolean;
140	};
141	
142	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
143	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
144	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
145	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
146	 *  already exports). */
147	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
148	
149	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
150	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
151	  if (!src) return undefined;
152	  return { src, alt: image?.alt ?? '' };
153	};
154	
155	/**
156	 * Picks the image group with the most images as this product's gallery. Ported near-verbatim from
157	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — viewpoint-agnostic on purpose, for the
158	 * same reason that file states: this catalog's real `viewType` naming was not confirmed for that
159	 * quick-test integration, so "most images" is used as a simple, real-data-driven proxy for "the
160	 * full gallery" rather than guessing a specific viewType string. Re-pointed at
161	 * `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape) in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own
162	 * same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image` types are identical either way, so only
163	 * the input type annotation changed. Returns `undefined` for 0 or 1 resulting images, matching
164	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for that case.
165	 */
166	export const selectGalleryImages = (
167	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
168	): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
169	  const groups = product.imageGroups ?? [];
170	  if (groups.length === 0) return undefined;
171	
172	  const largest = groups.reduce((best, group) =>
173	    (group.images?.length ?? 0) > (best.images?.length ?? 0) ? group : best,
174	  );
175	  const images = (largest.images ?? []).map(toCardImage).filter((img): img is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(img));
176	
177	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
178	};
179	
180	/**
181	 * Resolves the required `primaryImage` slot. Not ported from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
182	 * `toCardImage(hit.image)` — a plain `getProducts` `Product` carries no equivalent flat `image`
183	 * field, that's a Search-hit-only convenience. Mirrors `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own
184	 * `selectPrimaryImage` instead: `viewType: 'medium'` (a real, correctly-sized product image),
185	 * first matching group, first image, required non-empty `alt` (falls back to the product name) —
186	 * the already-established, correct approach for this exact input shape. `ZimmProductCardMedia`
187	 * ignores `primaryImage` entirely whenever `images` carries more than one entry (confirmed
188	 * directly in that component's own source — `slideImages = gallery ?? [primaryImage]`), so this
189	 * value never conflicts with `selectGalleryImages`'s independent, viewpoint-agnostic pick above
190	 * even on the rare product where the two would otherwise disagree on which image comes first.
191	 *
192	 * @returns `null` when there is no usable `src` — `ZimmProductCardMediaImage.alt` is required and
193	 *   non-empty, so there is no safe placeholder card to build without a real image, the same
194	 *   hard-gate contract `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectPrimaryImage` documents.
195	 */
196	const selectPrimaryImage = (
197	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
198	  productName: string,
199	): ZimmProductCardImage | null => {
200	  const filteredGroups = filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
201	    viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
202	    variationValues: {},
203	  }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[];
204	  const [groupImage] = filteredGroups[0]?.images ?? [];
205	  if (!groupImage) return null;
206	
207	  const src = groupImage.disBaseLink || groupImage.link;
208	  if (!src) return null;
209	
210	  const alt = groupImage.alt?.trim() || productName;
211	  return { src, alt };
212	};
213	
214	/**
215	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
216	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
217	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
218	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
219	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
220	 */
221	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
222	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
223	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
224	    value: value.value,
225	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
226	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
227	  }));
228	};
229	
230	/**
231	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
232	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
233	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
234	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
235	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
236	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
237	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
238	 */
239	const selectPriceFields = (
240	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
241	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
242	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
243	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
244	
245	  const currentPrice =
246	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
247	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
248	      : undefined;
249	
250	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
251	  // identical to its current one.
252	  const originalPrice =
253	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
254	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
255	      : undefined;
256	
257	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
258	};
259	
260	/**
261	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
262	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
263	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
264	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
265	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
266	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`.
267	 */
268	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
269	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
270	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
271	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
272	  if (!product?.name) return null;
273	
274	  const primaryImage = selectPrimaryImage(product, product.name);
275	  if (!primaryImage) return null;
276	
277	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
278	
279	  return {
280	    id: product.id,
281	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
282	    name: product.name,
283	    headingLevel: 'h3',
284	    primaryImage,
285	    images: selectGalleryImages(product),
286	    currentPrice,
287	    originalPrice,
288	    // Real, found gap -- see this module's own docblock's "Badge" section. ShopperProductsTypes.
289	    // Product carries no typed c_productBadges field, and there is no confirmation the plain
290	    // getProducts endpoint (as opposed to Product Search) populates this custom, index-only
291	    // attribute at all. Left unset rather than guessed at.
292	    badge: undefined,
293	    variation: 'plp',
294	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
295	  };
296	};

 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
 *
 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific
 * geometry/typography/variation values actually used here were independently verified, not taken
 * on the provisional source's word alone —
 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP`) was checked at two
 *     independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any bound variable —
 *     see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice, genuinely
 *     un-tokenised" citation.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.

 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span
          textStyle="heading3"
          color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"
          data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count"
        >
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>
      <chakra.div __css={styles.grid} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-group">
        {cards.map((card) => (
          <ZimmProductCard key={card.id} {...card} />
        ))}
      </chakra.div>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

534	### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write
535	
536	**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
537	step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
538	real bug if built as originally specced.**
539	
540	Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).
541	
542	This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
543	two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
544	isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
545	failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
546	the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
547	even means without Einstein.
548	
549	**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
550	revision.** The original design was:
551	
552	```
553	hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
554	```
555	
556	`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
557	Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
558	the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
559	registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
560	never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
561	cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
562	interim build. **Corrected logic:**
563	
564	```
565	hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
566	```
567	
568	— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
569	tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
570	storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.
571	
572	**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
573	markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
574	tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.
575	
576	- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
577	  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
578	  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
579	  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
580	  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
581	  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
582	- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
583	  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
584	- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
585	  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
586	  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.
587	
588	**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
589	session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
590	*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
591	plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
592	against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
593	reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.
594	
595	**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
596	for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
597	handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
598	assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
599	this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
600	the original design intent this section used to describe.
601	
602	**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
603	a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
604	(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
605	baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
606	once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.
607	
608	**Pass criteria**
609	- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
610	  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
611	  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
612	  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
613	- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
614	  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
615	- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
616	- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
617	  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
618	  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
619	  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
620	  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
621	- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
622	  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
623	  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
624	- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
625	  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
626	  refactoring upward).
627	
628	### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe
629	
630	Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
631	`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
632	`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
633

635	ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
636	`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test

638	
639	Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a

641	
642	**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
643	`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
644	carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.
645	
646	**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's

648

650	|---|---|---|---|
651	| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
652	| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
653	| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's
own AC text, and is **superseded, not merely refined**: the AC states plainly *"Confirmed surfaces
are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
interim design already.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR

**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
there.

**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
before touching it.

**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.

**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.

**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
intended to survive that swap unchanged.

**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
both interim, only one of which changes later:
1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.

**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
  change; only where the input object comes from does.
- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
  mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.
- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather
  than creating a duplicate entry — required for AC 2's "most-recent-first" to hold up under repeat
  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).
- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08, then SUPERSEDED same day once the 24-ID fetch limit
  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =
  500` was set as a generous engineering safety ceiling against unbounded growth. **That reasoning
  is now incomplete, not wrong** — it was correct given what was known at the time, but didn't yet
  account for two facts discovered later the same day: (1) Shopper Products `getProducts` has a
  hard 24-ID-per-request limit (SDK's own doc comment, independently confirmed twice during Phase 1
  implementation), and (2) Marcel decided the Full History page caps its fetch/display at 24 rather
  than batching (see B2 below). Given Full History will **never** show more than 24 items and the
  rail never shows more than 5, storing more than 24 serves no purpose — nothing beyond item 24 is
  reachable from any UI this build has. **`RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED = 24`, superseding
  the `500` above.** This was caught by Phase 1's own implementer, who read this plan directly,
  found the contradiction between what it was told to build and what this section said, and
  correctly surfaced it rather than silently picking a side — exactly the discipline this plan
  asks for elsewhere. **Open Question 17 is re-closed at the new number** — no further confirmation
  needed; this is a direct, logical consequence of Marcel's own 24-cap decision, not a new
  independent judgement call.

**What stays exactly as planned, unaffected by this whole section:** A2 (variation config), A5 (rail
UI), B1 (grid UI) — all purely presentational, receive cards as props, and have never cared where
those props came from. This is the container/presentational split (`components.md`) paying off
exactly as designed.

**To verify at implementation time, not guessed here:** the exact `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`
hook name for a batch product-detail fetch (likely `useProducts`, plural, alongside the already-used
singular `useProduct` — confirm against `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/dist/` per AGENTS.md's
own Gotchas note before trusting the name).

**Not a scope decision for this PR:** what the Einstein follow-up ticket looks like in detail (does
it reuse the `getProducts`-and-map layer, or fully replace it with `fetchRecProductDetails`'s own
internal enrichment?). Left for that ticket, once it exists — this section only needs to ship a
clean, honest interim, not pre-solve the migration.

### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
real bug if built as originally specced.**

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
  refactoring upward).
